The curvature on $\overline{\mathcal P}$ has minus the three vector-slot actions and plus $\rho^{(1)}$ on its conjugate canonical factor. Differentiating the sourced $Q$ equation and tracing gives
\begin{align*}
 \tau_{i\bar j}={}&\operatorname{tr}[(A_{\bar j}\mathsf J_i+(B_\eta)_{i\bar j}I/2)Q+M_i(D_jQ)^*]
 +\sum_{k,l,c}\varepsilon_{klc}J_{jk}^{c,il}\\
 &+\sum_{c,r}[(C_{\bar j})^{cr}\overline{\mathcal P^{c,ri}}
       +C^{cr}\overline{(\nabla_j\mathcal P)^{c,ri}}]\\
 &-\tfrac12\sum_{k,r}[(C_{\bar j})^{kr}\overline{\mathcal P^{i,rk}}
       +C^{kr}\overline{(\nabla_j\mathcal P)^{i,rk}}].
\end{align*}
At the chosen point $C=A$, but $C_{\bar j}$ must retain its full first-Bianchi value. Inserting the displayed first/second Bianchi equations and the preceding Ricci formula yields \eqref{c0:up:tauhessian} by epsilon contraction. These are identities of the unrestricted component arrays: $A$ is symmetric, $\mathcal P$ and $B$ are symmetric only in their last two indices, and $Q$ is Hermitian. The nine contractions use the same $B$ in both expressions. The source $B$ is never set to zero. Four times \eqref{c0:up:tauhessian} minus twice the norm identity proves \eqref{c0:up:hessian} at this point.

Under the pluriharmonic conformal change with $\varphi=0$ at the point,
\[
 \widehat p_{i\bar j}=p_{i\bar j}-\varphi_i p_{\bar j}-\bar\varphi_jp_i+p\varphi_i\bar\varphi_j.
\]
The first Ricci form is unchanged and the other pointwise quantities agree. Taking $\varphi_i=\eta_i/2$ restores \eqref{c0:up:hessian} in every gauge. Taking the trace uses full symmetrization of the three indices of $\mathcal P$.
<!-- end proof-126 -->
<!-- proof-127: body_md -->
Write $\beta_{\bar x}=\vartheta_x\ell$ on $V$.

\emph{Step 1: curvature normal form.} By \eqref{c0:eq:ricci}, $\nabla_y(\vartheta_x\ell)-\nabla_{\bar x}\bigl((\gamma_y-\frac12\eta_y)\ell-\varepsilon_y(r)\bigr)=R_{y\bar x}\cdot\ell$, where $\varepsilon_y(r)_b=\sum_c\varepsilon_{ybc}r^c$ and $\nabla_{\bar x}r=(\nabla_{\bar x}A)\ell+\vartheta_xr$. Modulo $\ell$ the terms $\vartheta_x\varepsilon_y(r)$ cancel and we obtain
\begin{equation}\label{c0:eq:Hol}
 \bigl(\varepsilon_y\bigl((\nabla_{\bar x}A)\ell\bigr)-R_{y\bar x}\cdot\ell\bigr)\wedge\ell=0\qquad\text{for all }x,y .
\end{equation}
At a point with $\ell=e^2$, insert \eqref{c0:eq:barA} and \eqref{c0:eq:decomp}; the $\mathcal P$-terms and the $\varepsilon_{x2d}Q$-terms cancel, and with $\sum_c\varepsilon_{ybc}\varepsilon_{xcd}=\delta_{yd}\delta_{bx}-\delta_{yx}\delta_{bd}$ the transverse components ($b\in\{0,1\}$) of \eqref{c0:eq:Hol} become
\[
 \delta_{xy}Q_{2b}-\delta_{bx}Q_{2y}+\sum_d\varepsilon_{x2d}\,\overline{\mathcal P^{d,yb}}=0 .
\]
For $x=y=2$ this gives $Q_{2b}=0$ ($b=0,1$); for $x\in\{0,1\}$ and $y,b\in\{0,1\}$ it gives $\mathcal P^{\alpha,\beta\gamma}=0$ for all $\alpha,\beta,\gamma\in\{0,1\}$; for $y=2$ it gives
\[
 \mathcal P^{0,02}=\mathcal P^{1,12}=0,\qquad \mathcal P^{0,12}=Q_{22},\qquad \mathcal P^{1,02}=-Q_{22}.
\]
Put $F_t=F\otimes K_X^{-1}\subset T^{1,0}X$ and let
$\ell^\sharp\in T^{1,0}X\otimes K_X$ be the Hermitian dual of
$\ell\in(T^{1,0}X\otimes K_X)^*$. The parallel identification
$\overline{(T^{1,0}X\otimes K_X)^*}\cong T^{1,0}X\otimes K_X$
includes the metric on $K_X$. There is a unique smooth tensor
\[
 n\in F_t\otimes T^{1,0}X
\]
such that, after moving the $K_X$ factor of $\ell^\sharp$ to the output slot,
\[
 \mathcal P=\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathrm{inputs}}(n\otimes\ell^\sharp),
 \qquad
 \mathcal P^{a,jl}=\tfrac12(\bar\ell_j n^{al}+\bar\ell_l n^{aj})
\]
in unitary frames of $T^{1,0}X$ and $K_X$. Here symmetrization is the
average of the two input placements. Under $\ell\mapsto g\ell$,
the factor changes by $n\mapsto\bar g^{-1}n$.
In the aligned frame above,
$n^{01}=2Q_{22}=-n^{10}$ and $n^{00}=n^{11}=0$.
If $Q_{22}=0$, then $\mathcal P^0,\mathcal P^1$ are both multiples of
$\bar\ell^2$ in that frame and $\operatorname{rank}\mathcal P\le1$; hence $Q_{22}\ne0$ on $V$.

\emph{Step 2: differentiating the antisymmetry.}
Let $b_h:T^{1,0}X\to\overline{T^{1,0}X}^{\,*}$ be the parallel,
complex-linear metric lowering map,
$b_h(x)(\bar y)=\langle x,y\rangle_h$. For the chosen annihilator
generator $\ell$, define
\[
 \mathcal B=(b_h\otimes b_h)(n)|_{\overline{F_t}\times\overline{F_t}}
 \in\overline{F_t}^{\,*}\otimes\overline{F_t}^{\,*}.
\]
In an adapted unitary frame,
$\mathcal B_{\bar\alpha\bar\beta}=n^{\alpha\beta}$
for $\alpha,\beta\in\{0,1\}$, so
$\mathcal B\in\Lambda^2\overline{F_t}^{\,*}$ on $V$.
Both $n$ and $\mathcal B$ have canonical-line weight zero and change
by $\bar g^{-1}$ under $\ell\mapsto g\ell$.
Since $F_t$ is $\nabla''$-invariant,
$\overline{F_t}$ is $\nabla'$-invariant. Parallel metric lowering
and restriction therefore commute with $\nabla'$, and
$\nabla'\mathcal B$ remains alternating. Write $\nabla_{\bar p}\ell=\vartheta_p\ell$.
Metric compatibility gives
$\nabla_p\ell^\sharp=\bar\vartheta_p\ell^\sharp$.
Differentiating the full tensor factorization and using
$\nabla_p\mathcal P=M_p^{(\mathrm{out})}\mathcal P$ yields
\[
 \nabla_p n=M_p^{(\mathrm{out})}n-\bar\vartheta_p n.
\]
The covariant derivative here acts on the two tangent slots of $n$;
the $K_X$ connection has already been retained in
$\nabla_p\ell^\sharp$. Consequently the $F_t\times F_t$ block
of $M_pn$ is alternating. With
$n^{e\beta}=2Q_{22}\varepsilon_{e\beta}$ for $e,\beta\in\{0,1\}$
and $\varepsilon_{01}=1$, its symmetric part is

\[
 p=2:\ \ 2Q_{22}\,A^{\alpha\beta};\qquad p\in\{0,1\}:\ \ -Q_{22}\bigl(r^\alpha\delta_{\beta p}+r^\beta\delta_{\alpha p}\bigr)\qquad(\alpha,\beta\in\{0,1\}).
\]
As $Q_{22}\ne0$, $A^{\alpha\beta}=0$ and ($\alpha=\beta=p$) $r^p=0$. Together with $A^{22}=q_{\ell}=0$ (Theorem~\ref{c0:thm:qzero}), $A=0$.
<!-- end proof-127 -->
<!-- proof-128: body_md -->
Set $L=2R+\eta_1$ and $D=6Rb+4R\varkappa{}+3b\eta_1$. Direct substitution of the structure equations and the pure solution above gives the following polynomial identity, with no unspecified remainder:
\begin{align*}
16R^2\varkappa{}^2\beta_{\bar2,1}={}&3R B_{29}+12aB_1-24bB_0-6R B_{21}\\
 &-4D\mathcal M_{12}^{02}-2D\mathcal M_{10}^{22}+24R^2\varkappa{}\mathcal Q_0\\
 &+12RL(\mathcal M_{12}^{01}+\mathcal M_{10}^{12}+\mathcal M_{11}^{02}+\mathcal M_{22}^{02})\\
 &+6RL(\mathcal M_{20}^{22}+\mathcal M_{02}^{00})+12RL\mathcal M_{00}^{02}\\
 &-6aL\mathcal M_{02}^{02}+2aL\mathcal Z_2^2-3aL\mathcal M_{00}^{22}
 -a\varkappa{}(R+2\eta_1)\mathcal Q_2.
\end{align*}
Every term on the right vanishes. Also $\mathcal Q_2=2R\beta_{\bar2,0}=0$. Since $R,\varkappa{}\ne0$, this proves $\beta_{\bar2,0}=\beta_{\bar2,1}=0$. The established first-order contraction $\varkappa{}\beta_{\bar\ell}-a_\ell\in\mathbb C\ell$ then gives the second assertion. The displayed polynomial combination, together with the four direct residual formulas, proves the required vanishing.
For precision, this is a complex polynomial certificate. The symbols
$B_0,B_1,B_{21},B_{29}$ name the four displayed combinations and are
not unspecified row numbers. The indices of $\mathcal M,\mathcal I,
\mathcal C,\mathcal Q,\mathcal Z$ determine every component used in
the certificate. Taking real and imaginary parts gives two real
identities with the same order of components. Formally,
$\bar\mathcal P$ and $\nabla'\bar\mathcal P$ can even be treated as independent
conjugate copies during the expansion: their coefficients cancel
without any additional conjugation constraint. The two entries
$\beta_{20}$ and $\beta_{21}$ remain unconstrained variables during
that expansion. Only afterward do the geometric residuals vanish,
giving $2R\beta_{20}=0$ and $16R^2\varkappa^2\beta_{21}=0$.
The required divisions are therefore by $R$ and $\varkappa$ only,
both nonzero on the open set in the lemma. The coefficient is
$\varkappa^2$, not $|\varkappa|^2$; nonvanishing suffices over $\mathbb C$.
No derivative of a specialized parameter value is set to zero.
